subject: Late-arriving transactions from replica failover — bridge letter scope and evidentiary manifest
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: security@clientco.com, David Lee <david.lee@clientco.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Dec 2024 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Late-arriving transactions from replica failover — bridge letter scope and evidentiary manifest

Hi David / security team,

During ClientCo's scheduled migration cutover yesterday we observed a database replica failover that caused a small window of delayed replication (roughly 30–90s) for a subset of writes. Your SOC 2 auditor flagged this as a potential point-in-time question and asked whether those late-arriving transactions should be considered inside or outside the attestation period.

To be proactive, we're preparing a short bridge letter that: 1) describes the operational event, 2) confirms which transactions are included in the period vs. considered post-period remediations, and 3) provides a manifest of the affected log records and their authoritative timestamps. I've attached a first-pass manifest (log_manifest_20241205.csv) showing UTC event times and the replication / commit timestamps, and a draft bridge letter will follow.

Quick asks:
- Can you confirm whether your auditor requires the bridge letter to state that the replica-delayed writes fall inside the period (as-of commit) or be documented as a post-period exception?
- Are the timestamps in the attached manifest (UTC commit_time vs. replication_time) acceptable as primary evidence, or do you need additional corroboration (e.g., storage-level WAL segments or network replication logs)?

We can tighten the language on the draft bridge letter to meet your auditor's expectations — cc’ing Marcus and Vanessa for any ops/forensics detail.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: log_manifest_20241205.csv (CSV, 54KB)

From: David Lee <david.lee@clientco.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, security@clientco.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Dec 2024 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Late-arriving transactions from replica failover — bridge letter scope and evidentiary manifest

Irene — thanks for the prompt.

We observed the same event on our side (replica promotion during the cutover). Our internal SEC/compliance lead asked whether the auditor wants the bridge letter to treat commits that show a later replication_time as within the period if the commit_time is inside the period. In practice we saw a handful of transactions where commit_time is 2024-12-01T23:59:45Z and replication_time is 2024-12-02T00:00:30Z.

Short answer: the auditor group said they accept authoritative commit_time as the determinative timestamp, but they often request explicit language clarifying the source of truth and why replication lag occurred. They also like a manifest and a short explanation of the mitigation (e.g., why this was limited to a single replica and how we prevented client impact).

Two follow-ups:
1) Can you add a sentence that the commit_time column is derived from the primary WAL record and is authoritative?
2) If you could include the incident ID from your ops runbook and a note about whether any user-facing requests were retried or failed, that would help our internal review.

Thanks,
David
David Lee
Head of Security Operations
ClientCo

David / Irene — adding ops detail and a draft bridge letter language below (attached as bridge_letter_draft.pdf).

Operational context (short):
- Incident ID: RGW-2024-11-30-OP-77 (failover triggered by network flapping to replica-2).
- Impact: ~78 write transactions observed with replication_time > commit_time spanning 2024-12-01T23:59:40Z through 2024-12-02T00:01:15Z.
- User impact: none — all client calls returned success; retry semantics in the application prevented duplicate exposure.
- Root cause mitigation: network path fixed and replica re-synced; WAL replays completed within 3 minutes post-failover.

Suggested bridge-letter language (high level):
"During the audited period ending 2024-12-01, Redwood experienced a targeted database replica failover that caused transient replication lag for a small set of writes. The authoritative source of truth for transaction occurrence is the database commit_time recorded in the primary's WAL. The attached manifest identifies the affected record ids and the corresponding commit_time and replication_time. No client-facing failures were observed and the condition was remediated within three minutes. The audit scope should consider transactions based on commit_time as the determinative timestamp."

I attached the draft as bridge_letter_draft.pdf and the manifest is the CSV you already have. Irene — happy to iterate wording if the auditor needs it tighter.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Site Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: bridge_letter_draft.pdf (PDF, 12KB)

Thanks Irene and Marcus — reviewed the draft and the manifest. This approach is acceptable in principle. A few items before we mark this closed on our side: 

1) Please include a one-line definition of "commit_time" (e.g., database primary WAL commit timestamp in UTC) and cite the log_manifest column name we should rely on.
2) Confirm the timezone/ISO format used (looks like UTC — state this explicitly).
3) Add a short statement that no customer-visible errors occurred and reference any incident ticket(s).
4) Provide a signed bridge letter (DocuSign link acceptable) and the final CSV manifest.

If you can send the updated PDF with the three clarifications and initiate the DocuSign template at the link below, we'll accept this as bridge evidence and annotate the SOC 2 workpapers accordingly.

DocuSign template: https://app.docusign.com/templates/s/eXampleDocSign

Thanks — once we have the signed letter and final manifest we'll close this item.

Best,
Ava Friedman
